creation.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Create a NEW ORIGINAL medical anatomical atlas illustration for a radiology learning site. It must be an anatomy illustration, not a paper figure, chart, MRI photograph, graph, or copied published image.
Subject: ONLY the corpus callosum in a true MEDIAN SAGITTAL SECTION of an adult human brain, anterior at LEFT, posterior at RIGHT. Isolate this single anatomical structure on a clean warm-white background. Omit all surrounding anatomical structures completely: NO cortex, thalamus, fornix, septum pellucidum, ventricles, cerebellum, brainstem, vessels, nerves, or extra tissue. Omission is intentional for anatomical accuracy.
Anatomical shape is paramount: a continuous broad C-shaped midsagittal callosal cut surface, long gently arched superior body/trunk, a smoothly rounded thick anterior genu curving inferiorly on the LEFT, a VERY THIN short tapering triangular rostrum extending POSTERIORLY (rightward) from the lower inner aspect of the genu, beneath it. The rostrum is the thinnest part, a flat tapered beak, NOT a thick curled tube, dangling hook, rope, or downward looping extension. The long body tapers through a narrowed posterior isthmus into a thick rounded posterior splenium on the RIGHT; the splenium is a local posterior bulb, not an elongated downward tube. The central body is distinctly thinner than genu and splenium. Approximate natural proportions: overall length 70 units, central body thickness 5 units, genu and splenium thickness about 10 units, rostrum thickness 1-2 units. The superior surface is one smooth continuous arch, not a semicircular horseshoe. Open space below the body; nothing fills it.
Rendering: restrained realistic medical 3D shading on a smooth matte ivory MID-SAGITTAL CUT FACE with very shallow depth only, like a carefully sculpted anatomical teaching specimen. Keep the camera perpendicular to the sagittal cut surface so landmarks cannot be distorted by perspective. NO invented surface fiber direction; specifically NO fibers running longitudinally around the C-shaped arch, no striated cables, ridges, grooves, or decorative textures. No visible colored regional borders: the tissue is one continuous ivory structure.
Composition: portrait 4:5, large central structure, ample whitespace for labels. Small simple title at top "Corpus callosum", subtitle "Mediansagittal · Midsagittal". Five precise thin callout lines terminating with small colored dots ON THE CORRECT PART of the callosal tissue. The lines do not cross. Each label appears exactly once, with a numbered circle at the start:
"1  Rostrum corporis callosi" / second line "Rostrum"
"2  Genu corporis callosi" / second line "Genu"
"3  Truncus corporis callosi" / second line "Body"
"4  Isthmus corporis callosi" / second line "Isthmus"
"5  Splenium corporis callosi" / second line "Splenium"
Line 1 MUST terminate on the thin short pointed beak below and behind the anterior genu; line 2 on the rounded left anterior bend; line 3 on the long central superior body; line 4 on the narrow transition just before the posterior bulb; line 5 on the rounded posterior bulb. Legible dark navy sans serif medical labels. Numbers 1 through 5 only. Small orientation labels "Anterior" on left, "Posterior" on right below the anatomy.
Avoid all additional anatomy or decorative visual details. The image must teach the gross anatomy of the single corpus callosum through an original anatomically plausible rendering. It is better to omit a detail than to invent it. No logo, watermark, publication attribution, MRI, measurement letters, scales, coordinate lines, or numerical measurements.

scope: Original simplified anatomical illustration of the isolated adult corpus callosum in midsagittal section.
review: Only the corpus callosum is depicted. Adjacent brain structures, vessels and detailed fibre tracts are intentionally omitted.
Anterior is left and posterior is right.
The rostrum is a short, very thin taper extending posteriorly from the inferior genu; it is not drawn as a hanging loop.
The anterior genu is rounded; the body forms the long superior arch; the posterior isthmus narrows before the rounded splenium.
Five leader lines terminate on the corresponding named callosal portions; Latin/German and English names were checked.
No quantitative normal measurements or sharply demarcated regional tissue boundaries are claimed.
replaces: A reproduced journal schematic/MRI figure, which did not match the user's request for an original anatomical illustration.
